description: Siemens SIPROTEC 4 7SA613 distance zones (Z1, Z2, Z3, Z4, Z5, Z1B) as a DIGSI 4 setting sheet prints them (address | name | value | range). Catalog-only. Configured settings: the per-zone Op. mode (status and direction, with 1201 FCT Distance), X(Zn) / X(Z5)+, RE(Zn) ph-E, Z1's Zone Reduction (tilt), the RE/RL - XE/XL compensation, the CT / VT ratings (units printed in the range column), the line data and the zone delays (an 'Infinity' setting is a configured value: the zone picks up but does not trip on its own timer). Documented relay behaviour (DEC-198, Siemens 7SA6 manuals C53000-G1176-C156-2 (V4.2) / -7 (V4.70), version-dependent for this V4.2-style parameter set): the polygonal (quadrilateral) characteristic and the phase-phase / phase-earth loops of every zone in service (no selector exists), the secondary-ohm setting basis, R(Zn) ph-ph as a per-phase value and the delay loop assignment. Source-data gaps: blank delay cells (Z1-Z3) and a blank load-cutout resistance. Not representable (blocking): the parallelogram's resistance edges inclined at the distance angle (+R and -R; exact relations preserved), a zone that only picks up (infinite delay), the non-directional Zone 5 polygon and a stated load cutout.
interpretation_notes: The zones are the sheet's Z1, Z2, Z3, Z4, Z5 and Z1B parameter groups (addresses 13xx); each zone's state and direction come from its own 'Op. mode' setting (Forward / Reverse / Non-Directional / Inactive), with the distance function itself (1201 FCT Distance) switched on.

Documented relay behaviour (Siemens SIPROTEC 4 7SA6 manuals C53000-G1176-C156-2, V4.2, and C53000-G1176-C156-7, V4.70): each distance zone is a polygon, 'a parallelogram which intersects the axes with the values R and X' tilted at the distance angle, symmetrical about the origin; the directional characteristic limits a directional zone to its quadrants, and a non-directional zone uses the entire parallelogram. A circle characteristic exists only on Region-DE devices (10th order-code digit A) through address 115, which this sheet does not carry; the V4.2 generation is polygon-only. Each zone measures the phase-phase and phase-earth loops (R(Zn) ph-ph / RE(Zn) ph-E); there is no per-zone loop selector. Applicability: this sheet's parameter set (Z1-Z5 + Z1B, R / X ranges 0.05-250 ohm, Zone Reduction 0-45 deg) matches the V4.2 manual; version-dependent, no firmware version is asserted.

Documented setting basis: secondary ohms. DIGSI 4 lets the settings be entered as primary or secondary values; the V4.2 settings table states its impedance ranges as secondary values for IN = 1 A, and this sheet prints exactly those ranges (0.05-250 ohms) for a 1 A device (CT SECONDARY 1 AMP; order code position 7 = 1), with its voltages and currents in secondary form (V, multiples of IN). Never inferred from the CT / VT ratios or from any magnitude.

Documented phase-phase geometry (per-phase R-X plane): R(Zn) ph-ph is a per-phase value (half the loop arc resistance), used directly; the right edge is Rright(X) = R + X * cot(phi) and the left edge Rleft(X) = -R + X * cot(phi), phi = the distance angle (1211, common to all zones); top X = X(Zn) (Z1 inclined downward in the first quadrant by Zone Reduction, 0 deg = horizontal); bottom -X; Zone 5 / 6 have separate forward (X+) and reverse (X-) reaches. The current engine draws vertical resistive edges, so neither edge is plotted while phi is not 90 deg. Approximation candidates A613 (+R = R, conservative, shortfall X * cot(phi)) and B613 (-R = 0 in the first quadrant, conservative where R >= X * cot(phi)) are documented only and not approved.

Delays: T-1phase is the zone's delay for single-phase faults, T-multi-phase for multi-phase faults; 'Infinity' is a configured value (documented: the stage then never trips on time). A blank delay cell is a missing source value: never Infinity, a range, a default or a note.

Load trapezoid (1241-1244, common to all zones): R load / phi load may cut the load area out of every polygon; R load = infinity switches it off. A blank R load (ph-ph) cell leaves its effect on the phase-phase plot unknown, so it blocks a zone in service. The phase-earth load cutout acts on the phase-earth loops, which the phase-phase engine does not draw.

zone_preserved.reason: The reverse reactance reach of non-directional Zone 5 (the parallelogram's bottom edge at -X(Z5)-). A non-directional zone uses the entire parallelogram, which the current engine cannot represent; preserved, not drawn.

Geometry-affecting: the phase-phase load trapezoid's minimum load resistance (1243), common to all zones; it cuts the load area out of the polygon unless set to infinity (Siemens C53000-G1176-C156-7, 2.2.2). Preserved; no value is assumed and no effect is claimed without it.
The phase-phase load trapezoid's maximum load angle (1244), common to all zones; it matters only with a finite R load (ph-ph). Preserved, not drawn.
The phase-earth load trapezoid (1241 / 1242), common to all zones: it acts on the phase-earth loops, which the phase-phase engine does not draw. Preserved, not drawn.
Loop selection for two-phase-to-earth faults (1221): which measured loops are evaluated, not the polygon boundary. Preserved, not interpreted.
The distance characteristic selector (address 115, Region-DE devices only). The documented polygon applies to the parameter set without it; a 'Circle' setting is not interpreted and blocks.

mappings.note: The zone is stated as X and R intersections (X(Zn), R(Zn) ph-ph, RE(Zn) ph-E), not as a polar reach. Its resistance edges are inclined at the distance angle, which this representation cannot carry (see the Right / Left Resistive Reach).
X(Z5)+: the forward reactance reach of Zone 5. Its reverse reach X(Z5)- is preserved with the zone.
Zone Reduction (1307): the inclination of Zone 1's upper limit in the first quadrant (Siemens 7SA6 manual); 0 deg = horizontal. Zones Z1B and higher have no such tilt.

gap.note: R({zone}) ph-ph is documented as a per-phase resistance reach (half the loop arc resistance), used directly, never halved (Siemens C53000-G1176-C156-7, 2.2.2.2). The zone is a parallelogram whose right edge is inclined at the distance angle phi (1211, common to all zones): Rright(X) = R + X * cot(phi), with R = R({zone}) ph-ph ({evidence}). The current engine draws only a vertical resistive limit (Rright = R), so this boundary cannot be represented exactly; no Right Resistive Reach (+R) is plotted and no approximation is applied. Only phi = 90 deg would make the edge vertical.

requires.off_note: The distance angle is not 90 deg, so the resistance edge is inclined and R ph-ph is not a vertical +R.
requires.missing_note: the distance angle (1211) was not found, so the inclination of the resistance edges is not established

mappings.note: R(Zn) ph-ph is a per-phase resistance reach, used directly (not halved; Siemens C53000-G1176-C156-7, 2.2.2.2). With the distance angle at 90 deg the resistance edge is vertical, so R ph-ph is exactly the Right Resistive Reach (+R).

gap.note: The polygon has a real left edge: the parallelogram is symmetrical about the origin, so Rleft(X) = -R + X * cot(phi), with R = R({zone}) ph-ph and phi the distance angle ({evidence}); a directional zone is further limited by the device's fixed directional characteristic (Siemens C53000-G1176-C156-7, 2.2.2.1, Fig. 2-22 / 2-24), a non-directional zone is not. The current engine cannot represent this edge; no left boundary is drawn, offered or approximated.

mappings.note: RE(Zn) ph-E, the polygon's R intersection for phase-earth faults, as printed: a per-phase value in the earth-compensated loop domain (RE/RL, XE/XL; Siemens C53000-G1176-C156-7, 2.2.2.2), its edges inclined at the distance angle like R ph-ph. Not drawn by the phase-phase engine.

T1-multi-phase is Zone 1's delay for multi-phase faults (Siemens 7SA6 manual): the phase-phase loop delay. 'Infinity' is a configured value (the stage never trips on time). A blank cell is a missing source value -- never Infinity, a range, a default or a note.

T1-1phase is Zone 1's delay for single-phase faults (Siemens 7SA6 manual): the phase-earth loop delay for single-phase faults. 'Infinity' is a configured value. A blank cell is a missing source value.
T2-multi-phase is Zone 2's delay for multi-phase faults (Siemens 7SA6 manual): the phase-phase loop delay. 'Infinity' is a configured value. A blank cell is a missing source value.

T2-1phase is Zone 2's delay for single-phase faults (Siemens 7SA6 manual): the phase-earth loop delay for single-phase faults. 'Infinity' is a configured value. A blank cell is a missing source value.
T1B-multi-phase is Zone 1B's delay for multi-phase faults (Siemens 7SA6 manual): the phase-phase loop delay. 'Infinity' is a configured value: the zone picks up but never trips on its own timer.
T1B-1phase is Zone 1B's delay for single-phase faults (Siemens 7SA6 manual): the phase-earth loop delay for single-phase faults. 'Infinity' is a configured value.
Zone 3's delay. 'Infinity' is a configured value (the stage never trips on time); a blank cell is a missing source value.
Zone 4's delay. 'Infinity' is a configured value (the stage never trips on time); a blank cell is a missing source value.
Zone 5's delay. 'Infinity' is a configured value: Siemens documents T5 = infinite as the way to keep the (non-directional final) stage from tripping. A blank cell is a missing source value.
